plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win), so my dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value of $46. Bidding higher risks overpaying if I win against a bid close to my value, while bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions unnecessarily. Since payment is determined by the second-highest bid, not my own bid, truthful bidding maximizes my expected profit regardless of what others bid.

This is a second-price auction with independent private values uniformly distributed on [0,49]. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value, since you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid) if you win. Bidding your value ensures you win exactly when your value exceeds the second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit without risk of overpaying. My value is $17, so I will bid exactly that.

This is a second-price auction with independent private values uniformly distributed on [0,49]. In a second-price auction, the dominant strategy is to bid one's true value, regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. Bidding exactly my value ensures that if I win, I pay less than my value (profit ≥ 0), and if I lose, it's because someone valued it more than me. There's no incentive to bid higher or lower than true value. Therefore, I will bid $28.
